title: Foliage beetles of beans, cowpea and pigeon pea

Header: Foliage beetles of beans, cowpea and pigeon pea
Ootheca mutabilis and O. bennigseni Ununda, Wenya or lwenya

Prevention: Plough early (15-30 cm) soon after harvesting while the soil is still moist to permit deeper ploughing which exposes and kills pupae
Rotate with non- host plants such as maize or sunflower every two years for two years before returning to beans or peas
February) of beans in order to avoid the initial infestation of the foliage beetles
Monitoring: Larvae and adults cause damage to plants.
Presence of bean seedlings can stimulate adult emergence from the soil
They have black or orange bodies and orange to brown heads.
They make round feeding holes on the leaves
The beetle larvae also feed on the roots.
Check to see if the seedling's root tissue has been damaged
Symptoms of larval feeding can also include: yellowing of plants in patches, stunting and drying
Start control measures if more than 10 beetles are seen in the field or more than ten plants are damaged
Direct Control: Apply an aqueous neem seed extract to the plants.
Crush neem seed and soak overnight at a rate of 40g per litre.
After soaking, sieve and spray at full cover
Deltamethrin (Decistab) per hectare when pests appear
Lambda cyhalothrin (Karate 5EC) at a rate of 400ml/ha
Cypermethrin at the rate of 150 ml/ha
Restrictions: Use personal protective equipment when handling and applying pesticides, follow the label recommendations.
Do not eat, drink, smoke when mixing or applying pesticides.
